blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Large language models often produce fluent but factually incorrect output. Gray-box detectors identify such hallucinations from the token-probability statistics emitted during generation, avoiding the need for white-box access to hidden states that frontier models do not provide. These detectors, however, typically rely only on probability-derived representations and ignore the identities of the candidate tokens. They can therefore observe how uncertain the model is, but not what it is uncertain about. Consequently, they cannot distinguish between a model that is torn between "big" and "small" and one that is torn between "big" and "huge" when the two pairs receive the same probability distribution.
  We introduce GURI (Gray-box Uncertainty Representations with Identity), a lightweight gray-box hallucination detector that combines candidate-token probabilities with per-token vector identifiers. This exposes which alternatives the model considered while preserving the accessibility and transferability of the gray-box setting. Across three open-weight models and three question-answering benchmarks, GURI increases mean test ROC-AUC from 72.09% to 79.09% over a probability-only baseline. On the closed-source GPT-4.1 model, mean ROC-AUC increases from 67.39% to 71.84%. Among the three open-weight models, GURI outperforms transferred probability-only baseline in 17 of 18 directed cross-model transfers without fine-tuning. For the three open-weight models, cross-dataset transfer between HotpotQA and TriviaQA with the model held fixed improves mean ROC-AUC over transferred LOS-Net by 3.76 points.

blocks.en:
Large language models can produce fluent but factually incorrect
responses, motivating methods for detecting hallucinations ( Ji et al., 2023 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Maynez et al., 2020 ) .
White-box detectors use internal model signals, whereas black-box
methods assess generated text, often using additional model calls.
Gray-box detection uses token probabilities exposed during generation
and can operate without internal activations or additional sampling ( OpenAI, n.d. ; Google, n.d. ) .

blocks.en:
The term “hallucination” has been used to describe several types of
erroneous model behavior ( Liu et al., 2022 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Ji et al., 2023 ; Rawte et al., 2023 ) .
Surveys distinguish factual inaccuracies from failures of faithfulness,
including contradictions and content unsupported by the provided
context ( Ji et al., 2023 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) .
Following the broad usage in error-detection research ( Orgad et al., 2025 ) , we use the term to encompass factual errors,
reasoning mistakes, and inconsistencies in model outputs.

blocks.en:
One class of approaches consists of black-box methods , which
operate on the model’s prompts and generated text. SelfCheckGPT
compares a response against additional sampled passages to identify
unsupported statements ( Manakul et al., 2023 ) .
Semantic-uncertainty methods group sampled responses by meaning before
measuring disagreement ( Kuhn et al., 2023 ; Farquhar et al., 2024 ) . Discrete semantic
entropy estimates group probabilities from sampling frequencies,
allowing text-only detection ( Farquhar et al., 2024 ) . White-box methods leverage internal model signals. These range
from probing classifiers ( Belinkov, 2022 ) trained on hidden
representations to predict correctness ( Azaria and Mitchell, 2023 ; Orgad et al., 2025 ; Snyder et al., 2024 ) , to more complex
architectures that process activation tensors across layers and tokens ( Bar-Shalom et al., 2025 ) , or combine activations and attention patterns ( Frasca et al., 2026 ) .
INSIDE provides another approach, measuring the diversity of internal
representations across sampled responses through their covariance
spectrum ( Chen et al., 2024 ) .

blocks.en:
Between these access settings, Gray-box methods use output-token probabilities without
hidden states or attention matrices. Earlier approaches include
length-normalized sequence likelihood for hallucination detection
in machine translation ( Guerreiro et al., 2022 ) and
P(True), the probability of an affirmative response when the model
is asked to verify an answer ( Kadavath et al., 2022 ) .
Related pipelines trigger external validation at low confidence ( Varshney et al., 2023 ) or combine and calibrate detection scores ( Valentin et al., 2024 ) . Semantics-aware methods include TokenSAR,
which weights generated-token log-probabilities by the semantic
effect of token removal ( Duan et al., 2024 ) , and
Claim-Conditioned Probability (CCP), which combines alternative-word
probabilities with entailment and contradiction judgments to
estimate claim-level uncertainty ( Fadeeva et al., 2024 ) .
Learnable methods include lightweight classifiers using summary
statistics of evaluator-model probabilities ( Quevedo et al., 2024 ) . LOS-Net ( Bar-Shalom et al., 2026 ) processes
sequences of actual-token probabilities and ranked candidate
distributions with a tailored architecture whose formulation can
approximate a broad family of prior probability-based scoring functions.

over candidate-token identities and probabilities. Its fixed random
identity codes retain information absent from probability-only representations, without requiring the explicit semantic similarity

blocks.en: 5 Discussion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 5. 讨论和限制

blocks.en:
Our results support token identity as a useful predictive signal beyond
next-token probabilities.

blocks.en:
The random-code results also require careful interpretation. The main random
construction retains the compositional structure induced by the external
tokenizer: target tokens that share external subtokens also share code
components. Accordingly, the experiments establish that pretrained semantic geometry is
unnecessary for the main gains, not that every form of lexical or tokenization
structure is irrelevant.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
GURI augments probability-only gray-box detection with fixed
token-identity codes while preserving its access and efficiency
advantages. Across our evaluation suite, it consistently improves
over LOS-Net. Fixed random codes perform comparably to pretrained
embeddings, showing that the gains do not require pretrained
semantic geometry. Channel ablations show that non-actual candidate
identities alone preserve full performance with random codes.
These results demonstrate the value of token identities for
hallucination detection beyond probability statistics.

Figure 8: Complete transfer results. Rows and columns denote source and
target model–dataset pairs: G, L, M denote Gemma, Llama, Ministral.
H and T are closed-book; N denotes open-book NQ-WC.
Bold values show test ROC-AUC (%); signed values and colors show
differences from target Confidence, listed above the columns.
Stars and outlines mark GURI scores above target-trained LOS-Net,
not statistical significance. Diagonal dataset blocks correspond to the
within-dataset cross-model panels in Figure 4 .
Each row uses one source-validation-selected checkpoint without
target fine-tuning.

blocks.en:
For the HotpotQA transfer from Ministral to Llama, GURI achieved
49.74 ROC-AUC, compared with 68.87 in the reverse direction.
A check confirmed that the low-scoring evaluation loaded the
3,072-dimensional target identity codes. This ruled out missing
identity codes as the explanation, but did not explain the result.
blocks.zh:
热点QA从内政部转至拉马,GURI实现了
49.74 ROC-AUC,相反方向为68.87。
检查确认,低评分评价加载
3,072-维目标身份代码. 这排除了失踪
身份代码作为解释,但没有解释结果。

eight A100-SXM4 GPUs with 40 GB memory each, 256 CPU cores,
